prediction.raw: 1 **Why:** In standard potluck etiquette, when you bring a dish to share, it’s understood that *if it’s not served or consumed*, you’re generally expected to take it home. The host here was rude for refusing to serve your lasagna (saying "nobody could compete with hers" to save you "from embarrassment" is unnecessarily condescending), and she didn’t even put it out for others to try. Since the dish was untouched and never part of the actual potluck spread, it remained *your property*. Taking it home was reasonable, especially as a broke college student who needed the food. Friends taking home untouched chips/pop further supports that this is acceptable behavior. The host’s expectation to keep it for "dinner tomorrow" is misplaced—she had no right to assume your unoffered dish was hers to claim. You were not the asshole.
